children: Indian equity indices snapped a four-day losing streak and ended higher on September 3, with the Nifty closing just below the 23,900 mark, led by buying across metal, oil & gas and private banking stocks.

Positive global cues and easing expectations of a US Federal Reserve rate hike at its upcoming monetary policy meeting supported the market opening. The Nifty crossed the 24,000 mark during the session, but intraday profit booking pared some of the gains with Nifty closing near to 23,900 after the Closing Auction Session (CAS).
At close, the Sensex was up 362.57 points or 0.48 percent at 76,515.43, and the Nifty was up 24.25 points or 0.10 percent at 23,897.70.
For the week, BSE Sensex and Nifty fell nearly 1% each.
The broader market traded mixed with Nifty Midcap index slipped 0.2%, while the Smallcap index gained 0.2% to hit a fresh record high.
Sector-wise, the Nifty Metal index was the top performer, rising more than 1%, followed by private banks and oil & gas stocks. Auto, IT, PSU Bank, pharma and realty indices declined around 0.5% each.

Among the Nifty gainers, SBI Life Insurance, Tata Steel, HDFC Life, Reliance Industries and Trent were the top performers, while HCL Technologies, Coal India, Maruti Suzuki, Bharti Airtel and Bajaj Finserv were the major laggards.

More than 180 stocks touched 52-week high including New India Assurance, IFCI, Maharashtra Seamless, Welspun Living, ACME Solar, Capri Global, Lenskart Solutions, Elgi Equipments, RBL Bank, Craftsman, Solar Industries, Redington, Usha Martin, PTC Industries, Anthem Biosciences, among others. Among individual stocks, Angel One rose 4% as gross client acquisition rose 19.9% , shares of Ramco System added more than 4% on signing MoU with Safran Helicopter Engines.

Sterlite Technologies added 5% after board approved a capex of Rs 3,000 crore for the company’s existing manufacturing facility and Polycab India shares shed 6% after JPMorgan kept an 'overweight' rating.

Shares of Shanthi Gears jumped 6% after board appointed Sai Krishna Alluri as CFO, while WeWork India share price added 2.5% after board has given in-principle approval for setting up a 10 MWp captive solar power plant in Karnataka.
The Indian rupee ended unchanged at ₹94.49 per dollar on Friday, compared with Thursday’s close of ₹94.49.
New Listings
Priority Jewels shares ended 20% higher at Rs 241 after making a strong debut on the NSE at Rs 230, a 15% premium to its IPO price of Rs 200 per share.

ESDS Software shares surged 111% to Rs 908 after a blockbuster debut on the NSE at Rs 757, representing a 76.46% premium over its IPO price. The company had fixed its IPO price band at Rs 408-429 per share.
Outlook for September 7
Rupak De, Senior Technical Analyst at LKP Securities

Nifty remained extremely sideways during the day as traders stayed on the sidelines ahead of the important US non-farm payroll and unemployment data, which could have a significant bearing on the Fed’s rate decision. The short-term trend is likely to remain weak as the index continues to trade below the 50-EMA on the hourly chart. A sell-on-rise sentiment may continue to prevail as long as the index remains below the 24,000–24,200 zone. On the lower end, support is placed at 23,830 and 23,700.
Sudeep Shah, Head - Technical and Derivatives Research at SBI Securities

On Friday, the benchmark index Nifty 50 witnessed a narrow trading range of 107 points and ended the session on a flat note, gaining 0.10%. On the daily timeframe, the index formed a small-bodied bearish candle with an upper shadow, reflecting indecision and a lack of clear directional conviction. Over the past five sessions, Nifty has traded within a range of nearly 348 points, highlighting continued consolidation until a decisive breakout emerges on either side.

From a technical perspective, Nifty continues to trade below its 20-day and 50-day EMAs, keeping the near-term structure cautious. The daily RSI remains in the 30–50 zone, indicating a lack of clear momentum, while the MACD continues to trade below the zero line, sustaining the negative bias. Meanwhile, the rising ADX indicates a gradual increase in trend intensity, suggesting that volatility may remain elevated with two-sided swings likely to persist.

Going forward, the 23750–23700 zone, which coincides with the 61.8% Fibonacci retracement level, is expected to act as a crucial support area. A decisive breach below 23700 could trigger further weakness towards 23600–23570 levels. On the upside, 24050–24080 will act as an immediate hurdle, while a sustained move above 24080 could trigger a pullback towards 24200 levels.
